interpretation: Every throughput case is within the 5 percent adverse threshold at its observed center; this is not an interval-based equivalence finding.
Five other target metric centers exceed the adverse 5 percent threshold, including pooled commit tail and lifecycle phases; all remain visible.
No ULMDB target has a Bonferroni-adjusted regression interval in this canonical campaign; wide intervals still allow material adverse changes in multiple metrics.
The path-separated IPv4 miss-tail pattern was not reproduced under the same canonical source/target paths; static matching instructions and layout control do not prove a universal causal explanation.
The engine field names cold/open/complete_cold_check describe a close/reopen journey with OS caches retained, not evicted-cache or physical cold-storage performance.
Sampled p99 values include timer overhead; per-case summaries combine trial/process p99 observations geometrically and are not pooled population quantiles.
The default engine is measured with the optional accelerator unused, so live-accelerator rebuild, memory retention, concurrency and application-level costs require separate evidence.
Native LMDB controls remain raw and unnormalized; no adverse case, phase or outlier was removed.
The strict all-metric admission gate is not clear, and automatic/default promotion cannot be justified as regression-free by this evidence.
